mappings.note: How pressure falls when the same force is spread over a larger area explains the force-area relationship. Not LO-102, because no everyday object is being designed or chosen.
How a liquid exerts pressure is the answer to the query about liquids and depth that LO-93 names verbatim. Not LO-95, which is kept for the general force and pressure concepts.
What a force can do, change speed, direction or shape, explains the effects of force. Not LO-91, because no kind of force is being distinguished.
Force defined as a push or a pull is the basic explanation of the concept. Not LO-91, because no contact/non-contact distinction is drawn.
Liquids pressing on the container walls is part of the liquid-pressure query in LO-93. Grouped with the other liquid-pressure items.
Atmospheric pressure named as the pressure of air explains the concept. Not LO-94, because no observation is being traced to it.
A rubber sucker sticking because of atmospheric pressure relates an everyday observation to its cause. Not LO-95, which covers what atmospheric pressure is.
The barometer as the instrument for atmospheric pressure is a measurement matter, and the frame's only measurement outcome, LO-97, covers angles alone. Cited at competency level for that reason.
Air rushing out of a punctured tube relates an observation to the pressure inside. Not LO-93, because no liquid is involved.
Why the weight of air does not crush us relates an everyday fact to balancing internal pressure. Not LO-95, because the item explains an observation rather than defining pressure.
Picking the non-contact force is the contact/non-contact differentiation named verbatim in LO-91. Not LO-95, because kinds of force rather than effects are at issue.
A boat stopping when rowing ceases relates the observation to resistive force. Not LO-95, because a real situation is being explained.
A football moving when force is applied explains the effect of force on motion. Not LO-94, because the item states the general effect rather than explaining a puzzle.
Picking the contact force is the contact/non-contact differentiation. Mirror of the non-contact item.
Pressure as force divided by area is the defining relationship. Not C-SCI2.3, which is cited only where units or instruments are asked.
Why knives and needles are made sharp applies the pressure-area idea to everyday tools. Not LO-95, because a design choice rather than the concept is the point.
Pressure rising with the height of the liquid column is the depth query LO-93 names. Grouped with the other liquid-pressure items.
Pressure rising as contact area shrinks is the force-area relationship. Not LO-102, because no object or use is named.
The unit of pressure is a measurement question, and LO-97 covers only angles. Cited at competency level for the same reason as the other unit items.
The instrument for measuring liquid pressure is a measurement matter with no learning outcome covering it.
Water rising into a released dropper relates an observation to atmospheric pressure. Grouped with the sucker item rather than with the definitions.
Pushing a rock as an example of muscular, contact force is the contact/non-contact differentiation. Not LO-95, because the kind of force is the answer.
A moving object changing direction when force acts explains the effect of force. Not LO-94, because the general rule rather than a puzzle is at issue.
A catapulted stone falling back because of gravity relates an observation to its cause. Not LO-91, because the item explains rather than classifies the force.
The SI unit of force is a measurement question with no learning outcome covering it, LO-97 being confined to angles.
Slipping on a banana skin explained by reduced friction relates an everyday event to its cause. Not LO-102, because nothing is being designed or chosen.
A camel walking easily on sand because its broad feet lower the pressure explains an observation. Not LO-102, because it is an adaptation rather than a human design choice.
Atmospheric pressure named as the pressure of surrounding air explains the concept. Duplicate in substance of the earlier item.
Pressure as force per unit area is the defining relationship. Duplicate in substance of the pressure formula item.
A push or pull being a force is the basic definition. Duplicate in substance of the force definition item.
Gravity named as the earth's pull identifies a kind of force, which is LO-91's business. Not LO-95, which covers what forces do rather than which kind acts.
Muscular force being a contact force is the contact/non-contact differentiation verbatim. Grouped with the other force-type items.
The force between charged bodies being electrostatic identifies a non-contact force. Grouped with the other force-type items.
What a force changes explains the effects of force. Duplicate in substance of the effects item.
The force from our muscles being muscular force identifies a kind of force. Grouped with the other force-type items.
Converting one kilogram weight into newtons is a measurement question, with no learning outcome in the frame covering units.
What a spring balance measures is a measurement matter, LO-97 covering angles only.
Deducing which boy pushes harder from the block's motion applies the idea of net force. Not LO-94, because the reasoning is about forces in general rather than an everyday puzzle.
Two opposing forces giving a net force equal to their difference explains how forces combine. Grouped with the net-force item.
The strength of a force being its magnitude explains how force is described. Not C-SCI2.3, because no unit or instrument is asked for.
